_comment: Which lav-mic part holds each camera clip, and where. t0_s = time in the mic part that lines up with the camera's first frame (measured: 3 probes at 4 kHz, then 7 probes at 48 kHz; within ~1 ms, no drift inside a clip). match_mic.py --map reads this and skips the search. client_id = Adnan's original (download these; they don't use our Drive quota), copy_id = our copy in RSV Video/Adnan (one raw + one mic part at a time — the video being edited and its mic part; copy_id is null for everything else). Add new shoots as new entries in 'shoots'.

2026-09-22.camera: Sony, 1920x1080 25 fps, recorded sideways (rotate ccw), camera audio pcm_s16be 48 kHz
2026-09-22.mic: lav 'MIC 3', 48 kHz 32-bit float mono, back-to-back 30-min parts (contiguous, sample-exact). Very quiet: about -40 LUFS, peaks near -14 dBFS
2026-09-22.clock_note: mic clock = camera clock + ~45 min 10 s (±1 s; camera timestamps are whole seconds)
